t: Fasilides chose Gondar as his royal camp in 1636, and it became the first permanent capital of the Ethiopian Empire, where he, Yohannes I and Iyasu I built castles and churches.
After Iyasu I died in 1706 the city declined as Tigrayan and Oromo power grew, and Ras Mikael Sehul seized it in 1767 at the start of the Zemene Mesafint.
Tewodros ordered it sacked in 1864 and the Mahdists attacked it in 1888 and 1889, leaving a town of ruins; the Italians occupied it in 1936, and it later became a provincial town.
dyk: Charles Poncet, the French physician of Iyasu I, was the first European to describe Gondar, in a Europe where Ethiopia was generally thought to have no fixed capital.
ev: Emperor Fasilides selects Gondar as his royal camp and begins its castle
Emperor Yohannes I orders Muslims and Jews to form their own sectors in the city
Iyasu I dies and the city begins to decline
Ras Mikael Sehul seizes Gondar, and the Zemene Mesafint follows
Tewodros orders the city sacked and his soldiers plunder its clergy and monasteries
Mahdist forces enter Gondar and burn its churches
Italian troops occupy Gondar without a fight
Forces of the EPRDF occupy Gondar in May

f.founded: In 1636 Emperor Fasilides selected Gondar as his katama (royal camp); the name Gondar had earlier been that of a regiment stationed to guard trade routes in the reign of Amda Seyon I.
f.where: In the North Gondar Zone of the Amhara Region of Ethiopia, about 35 km north of Lake Tana on the Lesser Angereb River and southwest of the Simien Mountains.
f.known: The capital of the Ethiopian Empire under Fasilides and his successors; the castles of Fasil Ghebbi; 44 churches; quarters for Muslims and for the Beta Israel; caravan trade from Sudan and the Red Sea; the sack of 1864; the Italian occupation of 1936
f.today: Gondar is a city and woreda of the Amhara Region, with the castles of Fasil Ghebbi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the University of Gondar.
